title: Technical English — Course 4, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 9

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the data-log demonstration take place?
tasks.audioText: The automation laboratory will demonstrate a sample data log on Friday at eleven. Students should bring the trend-chart worksheet. The instructor will show how a timestamp, measured value and equipment reference help describe a recorded event. The class will discuss how missing units or unclear time information can make a trend difficult to interpret.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which worksheet should students bring?

The instructor will show how a timestamp, measured value and equipment reference help describe a recorded event. tasks.prompt: A data log stores observations over time. A useful record includes a timestamp, the measured value, its unit and the equipment or sensor reference. When data are displayed as a trend, the time scale and axis labels help readers understand changes. Missing units or unclear timestamps can lead to incorrect conclusions, even when the recorded numbers are accurate. Reading 1. Which details should a useful data log include?
options: Supplier address, order quantity, delivery date and price
Operator name, shift date, training group and room number
Timestamp, measured value, unit and equipment or sensor reference
Machine colour, storage location, programme revision and tool number

tasks.prompt: How do time scales and axis labels help readers?
options: They show the equipment purchase price
They explain the supplier's delivery schedule
They replace the need to identify units
They help readers understand changes over time

tasks.prompt: Each data point ___ with a timestamp and unit.
Choose TWO fields essential to interpret a recorded numeric measurement in an automation data log.
A record that stores observations together with their time is a data ___.
A trend chart has no unit on its vertical axis. What should you say?
options: Could we add the correct unit so the measured values can be interpreted?
The chart is clear without labels.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of automation data logs in a logical order.
options: Display the data with clear labels
correctOrder: Display the data with clear labels

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining what information belongs in an automation data log and why timestamps and units matter.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: the response identifies relevant data-log fields such as value, source/device, timestamp and unit (0–2); it explains how timestamps and units support interpretation and comparison of records (0–2); the explanation is clear with understandable grammar (0–2); automation/data-log vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are accurate (0–2).
